_comment: User-adjustable drafting/manufacturing conventions. The reader and the recipe read these instead of re-deriving them per drawing — settling a convention here is cheaper and safer than making the model reason about it every time (a wrong guess builds VALID but mirrored geometry).
_projection: first_angle (ISO/European, set 2026-07-27) | third_angle (ASME/American). Decides which physical face a placed view shows. FIRST: the view BELOW the front view is the TOP view, and the object's BACK is at that view's TOP edge (adjacent to the front view). THIRD: mirror of that. Samples f-1 = third_angle (drawn before the switch); f-2 / s-2 = first_angle.

sheet_metal._k_factor: Neutral-axis factor used when converting bent-state dimensions to a flat blank and back. 0.5 = the SolidWorks default, VERIFIED on s-1 and s-2 to 6 decimals. If a drawing's own flat pattern disagrees with the arithmetic, the reader FLAGS it (k_factor_mismatch) rather than silently re-deriving.
sheet_metal._bend_note_pattern: Flat-pattern bend annotation. Locale is NOT translated by SolidWorks (user-confirmed: always UP/DOWN).
sheet_metal._bend_class_map: Which EDGE CLASS a bend line of each direction is drawn with. SolidWorks views the flat pattern from one side, so a bend folding away is an obscured edge. This is the second, independent channel that identifies WHICH line a note annotates (recipe R10) — stated here rather than hardcoded because it is a drafting convention, not a law.
sheet_metal._bend_flip_map: Which UP/DOWN direction needs the sketched-bend `flip` flag. WHICH WAY SolidWorks folds depends on the sheet's INTRINSIC orientation (set by the base flange's thickness-direction flags, IR-ADR-014), not on anything the drawing says — so this is a build convention that pairs with reverse_thickness=false, verified by rebuilding s-1/s-2 and comparing. Flip these two booleans if a rebuild folds the mirrored way.
sheet_metal._bend_note_max_offset_mm: Safety net: a candidate line further than this (in PAPER mm) from its note is not a candidate at all. Observed offsets on s-1/s-2 are 4.51-4.52 mm, so 25 is ~5x headroom.
sheet_metal._note_above_bend_line: The UP/DOWN annotation sits ABOVE the line it annotates, along the note's own local up axis (its DXF rotation). Candidates are therefore restricted to lines PARALLEL to the note's baseline on the NEGATIVE side of that axis. VERIFIED 6/6 on s-1 + s-2 (all offsets 4.51-4.52 mm, rotation 0). The ROTATED-note case is untested — see logs.md KNOWN RISKS.

tolerance._cluster_gap_mm: Bounding-box gap below which two primitives are treated as one view cluster.
tolerance._chain_eps_mm: Endpoint-coincidence tolerance for contour chaining. Deliberately looser than coord_eps_mm (0.001 is inside DXF float noise) and far below any real feature.

curve_fit._fit_eps_paper_mm: Exploded curve fans (a tilted hole's ellipse written as 48 LINEs by the DXF exporter) are collapsed to ONE parametric ellipse only when the whole polyline — vertices AND chord midpoints — lies within this distance of the fitted curve. PAPER mm, multiplied by the view's own scale, because the exporter tessellates on paper: measured sag 0.011 (f-3) and 0.019 (s-6, a different document's image-quality setting). 0.03 = 1.6–2.8x those; a 24-gon drawn at 5 mm paper radius sags 0.043 and is refused, so a polygon stays a polygon. Decided with the user 2026-09-03.
curve_fit._min_segments: A run shorter than this is never fitted: 5 points determine a conic EXACTLY, so a 4-segment run fits a WRONG ellipse inside the sag (measured 4.916 for a true 5.000 on f-3). Eight segments = nine points for five unknowns.
curve_fit._max_turn_deg: Consecutive chords of a curve turn by less than this (a 12-segment ellipse turns 30 deg per chord); a chamfer (45) or a hexagon (60) never enters a run.
curve_fit._min_sweep_deg: A fitted ARC is emitted only when it sweeps at least this much (parametric degrees). The residual proves the curve passes through the points, not that its parameters are DETERMINED: on synthetic fans with the exporter's own sag, a 45-60 deg arc fits the semi-axes 2-9% wrong, a >= 90 deg arc <= 0.65%, a half ellipse 0.03% (measured 2026-09-03; f-3's 53 deg boss arcs read rx 11.5 for a true 12). Shorter arcs stay raw.
